# People action lifecycle

People `useAction` reuses `createPlanningScope` for one pending operation per resource.
A render that replaces the scope disposes the old resource immediately. A layout
cleanup disposes the mounted resource synchronously during component removal, even
when mount, scope replacement, action and unmount finish before passive effects run.
Disposal is terminal: it aborts the current signal, invalidates completion ownership
and refuses further submissions through a retained action function. The guard's
existing idempotent disposal and duplicate-admission semantics are unchanged.

Only a current owner may deliver success, error, completion callbacks or the latest
consumer callback. Current successful and failed actions still settle normally. An
old action's `finally` cannot finish a newer operation. Local abandonment cannot undo
a mutation the server already accepted; refresh current state before deciding again.

The maintained pinned Chromium lifetime case in
`packages/web/test/people-admin-browser.test.js` uses the actual Preact hook. Within
one animation frame it mounts an action, optionally replaces its scope, starts a
pending request and removes the component. A MutationObserver records DOM removal,
requires that the final scope's passive setup has not run, and releases success or
error at that boundary. The regression requires an already-aborted signal, no
completion/effect delivery and no retained-function reentry. Its existing duplicate,
current success/error, opaque-resource and first-render paging assertions remain.
No sleep or expanded browser deadline establishes the ownership boundary.
